Tell us all about your favorite characters you've played!

My favorite character is one I haven't actually got to play yet, but he's a 5e Fiend Pact Warlock with the sage background. I imagine him looking a lot like Hugh Laurie. His name is Gregori Lock, and he was originally just a man who researched fiends and devils as a profession, summoning them for interviews and experiments in the like and would teach at a mage college about demonology and fiends. His wife was a cleric who assisted in keeping the evil entities restrained and in check during the experiments. Eventually his wife fell sick and Gregori decided to summon an archfiend's servant and traded his soul for a cure, but in true fiendish fashion the substance used to cure his wife while indeed getting rid of her disease was also a deadly poison. Gregori Locke now travels to find a way to redeem his soul, and to further his research into the weakness of devils to get revenge on his new devil overlord.

That'd be my 3.5e Sun Elf Wizard/E.Savant/Archmage. Raised as a slave and earned his keep teaching. During our first session we had to infiltrate a guard house for evidence of paperwork forging and we were spotted. Our monk had the good sense to slam the bunkroom door and topple a book shelf in front of it. I'd panicked at the thought of death so I set the shelf on fire, burning down most of the guard house in the aftermath. A few more sessions in and we're now somehow political double agents. I was told to find a way from the front lines of one army to the command camp of another. I opted for flight. While crossing I noticed things seemed to be in pretty much a stale mate as the larger army actually held the only way across a large river. I was supposed to be aiding the smaller one anyways so I firebombed their outposts on their side of the river and the center of the bridge.

Move deeper into the campaign and I've now earned rank during my political travels and I'm an archmage finally. We're sent on a high profile assassination mission as we've located the murderer who killed the king who's successor would go on to betray us in a big way. Before the fight my character learns that this killer is actually my character's sister and his exact build opposite. Where I am a Fire/Positive energy Savant and Archmage she was a Cold/Necrotic savant and Dark Scholar.She'd nearly killed me during the encounter too, if it hadn't been for our Monk saving me from her zombies and our Fighter putting an arrow strait into her heart.

My very first character Leokul. He was a halfling ranger that took a lot of risks and didnt think about consequences. He nearly died several times from unlucky rolls, or falling out of 10ft tall tree's, or running in arrows flying into fights. Ultimately it was a box that killed him. We were on a mission to collect all these gems to help in the fight to killing the bbeg. As he found a small wooden box after a fight, he got too eager and opened the box without someone translating the letter that was with it. Turns out the box needed a code word otherwise you just turned into ash.

Favorite of all time, bar none, including any theoretical future characters, is Eepa the paladin. I say this because he was a character that I had a plan for and he looked at that plan, laughed, and did his own thing.

The campaign was a premade the DM was running (and modding the shit out of) called the kings bones. There's an NPC you can meet called bigguard, unless it was my DM modding in which case nvm. So bigguard was a choker, an abberation, but he was kinda cute in the simple little kid way. So my pally began giving him food and rolling/rping diplomacy to make him not evil.

I had gotten him up to lawful neutral when it happened. We were mobbing down the hallway when a wererat rogue popped out of the shadows and was finn ta squab. So the battle is going not well, we will probably win but somebody is gonna die, Eepa is front lining and taking hits for the team so he's most likely to die.

I had accepted it and my only regret was not being able to see bigguard become a warrior for justice, and then I did. Bigguard took his first and only action in the combat, bull-rushing the rat off the nearby stairs and saving me. In a panic I charge and leap off the stairs, fail my check and trip prone.

Get to my feet in time to see bigguard get his neck torn open.

I enter a palading rage, burn every smite evil I have and solo kill the rat hating it every round it doesn't drop because that's one more point bigguard slips to -10. I finally drop the rat and throw my sword away as I drop to my knees, no standard action to spare pulling out my healers kit. I roll to stabilize, I fail.

Bigguard hits neg ten while I cry over him.

I swear loudly IRL and in game. Pick up sword and dismember rat that is unconscious but not dead.

Drop sword and start swinging.

Punch rat until I've gone through and I'm punching stone.

Keep going until gantlet is ruined.

Take bigguard and leave group to make his cairn.

Don't sleep for three days doing this.

Finally sleep, level up. New paladin level gives lay on hands. Have dream about bigguard walking through door with holy symbol of my god (heironeous).

Had to step outside to smoke and punch the wall, and cry. Changed entire tone of my paladin and my plans for him. Stop ranking up jump and climb, everything is diplomacy and heal. Find and murder the everliving shit out of the guy that had hired the rat. He asks for mercy, I look at him and say "bigguard" before defenestrating him.

Actually just stabbed in face but defenestrate is a fun word.
